sources.title: Berkowitz, Bour, Davy & Odling (2000) Scaling of fracture connectivity in geological formations. GRL 27(14), 2061-2064
sources.used_for: Connectivity framework for the topology candidate class (exponent a, fractal dimension D, density, critical length)
sources.status: Publisher abstract rechecked this session; full text read previously via a ResearchGate copy.
sources.evidence: Abstract: connectivity depends on scale of measurement for a < D+1, independent of scale for a > D+1; "Analysis of the San Andreas fault system shows that a < D+1 and that the connectivity threshold is reached only at a critical length scale." Text: a = 2.1, D = 1.65, beta = 0.0085; "connectivity is expected for L > 21 km"; "the above results are statistical, and provide connectivity estimates on averages, rather than on particular realizations". Publisher abstract states that connectivity depends on a, D and density, with scale behavior conditional on a relative to D+1; it does not validate any individual candidate gap.

sources.title: Hermant, Kiersnowski & Bellanger (2025) Using Deep Learning to Map Quaternary Faults in Western USA. Proc. 50th Workshop on Geothermal Reservoir Engineering, Stanford University (SGP-TR-229)
sources.used_for: Benchmark background and contextual motivation to test, not assume, an offset annulus: Fig. 2 reports that a local USGS-QFaults/TLS-lineament separation can be up to 400 m. It does not establish a typical offset distribution or validate H27-10's 100-300 m band.
sources.status: full PDF fetched and read via the page-fetch service on 2026-10-02; Fig. 2 wording supports a local separation up to 400 m. It does not establish a general 150-400 m distribution, a 150 m lower bound, or the H27-10 100-300 m annulus.
sources.evidence: The official PDF's Figure 2 says local distance between USGS Quaternary faults and TLS fault labels can be up to 400 m. This is a reported local upper example, not a distribution. It does not validate a 100-300 m target ring. The paper also reports FaultSEG PR-AUC 0.595 vs siUNET 0.449 and documents false positives from geomorphic features; neither result is a direct validation of this repository's candidate.
